newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed, dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed, dull trade.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed after a quiet day, with players unwilling to commit in the absence of leads and lack of overseas participation.
Traders said the market was waiting for enquiries from Europe as the summer holidays are approaching to an end.
"We are waiting for Europeans to come in to buy as factories are resuming operations," a dealer at a trading firm said, adding that only light scattered Asian enquiries were seen for SMR grades.
Trading activity was thin as players awaited leads at the start of the week, dealers said.
The closure of the Japanese markets for a holiday also limited activity, traders said.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board set indicator price for Oct RSS1 buyer at 328.50 cents ($1.32) a kg, down half cent from Friday. Oct SMR 20 buyer rose a cent to 315 cents a kg.
The INRO five-day moving average was 250.24 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Sept 13 from 250.45 on Sept 12. The daily indicator price was 250.37 against 250.30.
